text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A joint censure motion of three opposition parties aiming to topple the Islamist-led government has been submitted to the parliament.
- Turkey will build up its first gold refining factory in Istanbul. The factory will annully turn 15 tonnes of gold into jewellery.

- Conservative State Minister Isilay Saygin is expected to present her resignation on Saturday. Two other conservative ministers have already quit the coalition, charging the partnership with the Islamists has damaged the country.
- Defence Minister Turhan Tayan in meeting with Turkish businessmen said the military would like to raise its use of Turkish-made equipment to 40 percent from the current 21 percent.
- A court reinstated the Turkish police chief back, ivalidating a decision by the interior minister to sack him.
- Private channel ATV opens new building, "ATV 2000".
- Government partners adopt populist policy in economy in order to hunt votes as expectations grow of an early election.
- Turkey's annual tourism revenue has grown by 1,500 percent since 1980.
- Opposition parties are in a quest for the necessary 276 votes to would topple the Islamist-led government.
- The government has begun work on a mid-term stability package to present to the IMF.
